headline: Shift Data Center Energy Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill shifts certain electricity infrastructure costs, including capacity auction costs and potentially new distribution infrastructure, onto large energy users like data centers and manufacturers, aiming to reduce residential electricity bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: State Senator Louise Lucas, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Dominion Energy (initially), consumer advocacy and utility watchdog organizations, U.S. Sen. Mark Warner.
opponents: Data Center Coalition (concerned about language), Governor Abigail Spanberger (suggested alterations).
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a key energy measure designed to shift more costs onto data centers to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics, including Dominion Energy, argue the amendments undermine the original goals of lowering costs for customers and expanding energy assistance.

headline: Require Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water users providing water to data centers report monthly or quarterly water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board, with data becoming publicly available.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Liz Guzman (sponsored similar measure HB496), The Piedmont Environmental Council, Friends of the Rappahannock, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry (initially questioned being singled out).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public.
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality, making the numbers publicly available. This aims to address concerns about data center water consumption, despite the industry's claims of low overall state water usage and efforts to reduce it.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Impact Assessments
short_summary: This bill requires new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to conduct site assessments for noise impact on nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to require assessments of impacts on various environmental and historical resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Josh Thomas, Senator Danica Roem (sponsored identical SB 94), The Piedmont Environmental Council, Virginia Conservation Network, local communities.
opponents: Not explicitly stated in search results.
news_headline: Committee backs noise assessments for large energy facilities.
news_summary: House Bill 153, which requires site assessments for noise impact from high energy use facilities like data centers on nearby homes and schools, was reported by the Committee of Counties, Cities and Towns. The bill also allows localities to require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forestland.
